llm.summary: The skill appears to implement a Notion-based long-term memory system, but its declared metadata and runtime instructions are inconsistent (missing required env/config declarations, mismatched command examples, and heavy use of local execs), so you should review credentials, required companion skills, and the scripts before installing.

dimensions.detail: The declared description (Notion LTM / emotion/state / journal) matches the included scripts and README: the code actually creates Notion DBs, writes/queries pages, and manages emostate/journal entries. However the registry metadata claims no required env vars or config paths while SKILL.md and the scripts explicitly require a Notion token (NOTION_API_KEY / NOTION_TOKEN) and a local config at ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json. Also SKILL.md command examples call python scripts (ltm_write.py, ltm_search.py) but the package contains .js Node scripts, a mismatch that could confuse users or cause runtime errors. Overall capability is coherent with the description, but the metadata/instruction mismatches are a red flag.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts operate on Notion via a local helper (notionctl) and will: read ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and workspace IDENTITY.md, create and patch Notion databases under a parent page, write ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json, append local logs (skills/.../state/*.jsonl), and call other local skill scripts. They do not call arbitrary external servers beyond Notion (via notionctl) but they do execute local Node child processes (execFileSync). The agent is instructed to use an external builder skill for subagent payloads but local planner code remains present. The instructions are fairly prescriptive (not open-ended), but they reference files and configs that the registry omitted — review those file accesses and companion skill dependencies before use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no network download/install spec in the registry (instruction+code bundle only). That reduces supply-chain risk from remote downloads. However the scripts expect other local skills (notion-api-automation and subagent-spawn-command-builder) and call a notionctl script via execFileSync, which means behavior depends on code in those companion skills; you should verify those are the intended, trusted implementations.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires a Notion integration token (NOTION_API_KEY / NOTION_TOKEN) and reads/writes local config (~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json) and OpenClaw workspace config (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json / IDENTITY.md). The registry metadata did not declare any required env vars or config paths — that is a substantive mismatch. Requesting a single Notion token is reasonable for a Notion LTM skill, but the missing declaration plus access to workspace config files and ability to run local notionctl child processes increases the effective credential/scope the skill will have. Ensure you provide a minimal-scoped Notion integration and verify the skill's code before granting access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always:true and uses the platform default allowing model invocation. It writes its own config file and logs under ~/.config and skills/state (normal for local skills). There is no indication it modifies other skills' configs or requests permanent system-wide privileges. Because it can run autonomously and has access to a Notion token, exercise caution — autonomous invocation combined with credential access raises the blast radius, but this is not unique to this skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill implements a Notion-based long-term memory and includes real code that will run on your machine. Before installing: 

- Expect to provide a Notion token (NOTION_API_KEY or NOTION_TOKEN) and to allow the skill to create/read/write databases under a parent page; the registry metadata did NOT declare these — treat that as an omission and verify manually.  
- Verify the companion skill 'notion-api-automation' (provides notionctl) and 'subagent-spawn-command-builder' are installed and trusted: the scripts call notionctl via node child processes (execFileSync), so whatever notionctl does will run with your environment and credentials.  
- Inspect the included scripts yourself (they are present in the bundle). Pay attention to setup_ltm.js, notionctl_bridge.js and ltm_common.js which read ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and IDENTITY.md and will write ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json and append logs to skills/*/state. If you want isolation, run this skill in a disposable/testing workspace or container.  
- Use a dedicated Notion integration token with minimal permissions (only the databases/pages needed) rather than a broad personal token.  
- Note the SKILL.md examples call .py scripts that are not present (the bundle contains .js): check and correct usage before running commands.  

If you want me to, I can: (1) list the exact places the code reads/writes local files and env vars, (2) rewrite the SKILL.md commands to match the provided .js scripts, or (3) outline a minimal Notion permission set and step-by-step safe install/checklist.
